entities.summary: Aulus Cornelius Cossus Arvina, a Roman statesman and general, played a pivotal role in shaping the late Roman Republic. Born around 370 BC, he rose through the ranks of the Roman army, becoming consul and Magister Equitum twice, and Dictator in 322 BC. His leadership during the Macedonian Wars and his strategic alliances with other Roman leaders helped maintain Roman dominance in the region. Despite his significant contributions to Roman politics and military strategy, Aulus Cornelius Cossus Arvina's legacy was largely overshadowed by that of his contemporaries, such as Scipio Africanus and Appius Claudius Caecus. His importance lies in his ability to navigate the complex web of alliances and rivalries that characterized the late Roman Republic, and his eventual rise to power serves as a testament to his skill and determination. Through his actions, Aulus Cornelius Cossus Arvina left a lasting impact on Roman politics and society, one that would be felt for generations to come.
